abstract: |
  Quantifying the space use of the pigs in East Alligator, and how that changes across seasons and for different months of the year. For estimating space use we are using 'occurrence' distributions, which are the probability of finding an animal in a given area at a given time. This is different to 'range' distributions, which are the probability of finding an animal in a given area over a long period of time (i.e. their home range). Occurrence distributions are more appropriate for short-term space use, such as across seasons and months.
---

# Load packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
packages <- c("amt", "lubridate",
              "ctmm",
              "terra", "sf",
              "beepr", "tictoc",
              "leaflet", "viridis")
walk(packages, require, character.only = T)

# prevent scientific notation in outputs
options(scipen = 999)

```

# Create directories for outputs

```{r}

# general outputs directory
outputs_dir <- "outputs/east_alligator/space_use/"
dir.create(outputs_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

```

# Import GPS tracking data

```{r}

pig_all_steps <- read_csv("data/pigs_east_alligator_steps_covs_20261015.csv")

# Convert timezone after import (resets to UTC)
pig_all_steps <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  mutate(
    t1_  = with_tz(t1_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin"),
    t2_ = with_tz(t2_, tzone = "Australia/Darwin")
    )

```

## Get into format for ctmm

```{r}

# keep relevant columns
pig_all <- pig_all_steps %>% 
  dplyr::select(name, t1_, x1_, y1_, date, month, season)

head(pig_all)

```

## Select a subset of the data for prototyping

```{r}

pig_subset <- pig_all %>% filter(month == 11) 

# choose which dataset to use
pig_data <- pig_subset
# pig_data <- pig_all

```


## Convert to ctmm telemetry object

```{r}

# as.telemetry() identifies columns by their Movebank names, so we rename them.
# x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert (EPSG:3112), so convert to WGS84 lon/lat
pig_data_movebank <- pig_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(x1_), !is.na(y1_), !is.na(t1_)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  mutate(location.long = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
         location.lat  = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(ID = name,
            timestamp = t1_,
            location.long, location.lat,
            month, season) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# returns a list of telemetry objects, one per individual
pig_data_ctmm <- as.telemetry(pig_data_movebank,
                             timezone = "Australia/Darwin",
                             keep = c("month", "season"))

```

# Pull out one pig for visualisation and testing

I am using the tutorial at <https://ecoisilva.github.io/AKDE_minireview/code/AKDE_R-tutorial.html> to estimate home ranges over the full tracking period.

## Betty

```{r}

pig_betty <- pig_data_ctmm[["Betty"]]
plot(pig_betty)

```

## Check range residency

We can see that Betty's variogram is asymptotic after a very short period, indicating that she is range resident.

```{r}

level <- 0.95 # we want to display 95% confidence intervals
xlim <- c(0,2 %#% "month") # to create a window of 2 months

SVF <- variogram(pig_betty)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(SVF, fraction = 1, level = level)
# abline(v = 0.1, col = "red", lty = 2) # adding a line at 1 month 
plot(SVF, xlim = xlim, level = level)
# abline(v = 0.1, col = "red", lty = 2)

```

## Selecting a movement model

```{r}

# Calculate an automated model guesstimate:
GUESS1 <- ctmm.guess(pig_betty, interactive = FALSE)

# Automated model selection, starting from GUESS:
FIT1_ML <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, method = 'ML')
FIT1_pHREML <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, method = 'pHREML')
## reminder: it will default to pHREML if no method is specified.

summary(FIT1_ML)
summary(FIT1_pHREML)

```

### Checking model selection

```{r}

FIT1_pHREML_verbose <- ctmm.select(pig_betty, GUESS1, verbose = TRUE)
summary(FIT1_pHREML_verbose)

```

## Providing a movement model to the home range estimator

```{r}

# Run an area-corrected AKDE:
UD1_ML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_ML)
UD1_pHREML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_pHREML)

summary(UD1_pHREML)$CI # home range area estimation

```

## Diagnostics

```{r}

summary(UD1_pHREML)$DOF["area"] # effective sample size of Betty
nrow(pig_betty) # absolute sample size

```

## Weighted AKDE for comparison

```{r}

UD1w_pHREML <- akde(pig_betty, FIT1_pHREML, weights = TRUE)
summary(UD1w_pHREML)$CI # home range area estimation (weighted)

```

## Plotting estimated home ranges

```{r}

# Creating an extent that includes both UDs at the 95% CI level:
EXT <- extent(list(UD1_ML, UD1_pHREML, UD1w_pHREML), level = 0.95)

# Plotting pHREML (with and without weights) side-by-side:
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(pig_betty, UD = UD1_pHREML, ext = EXT)
title(expression("pHREML AKDE"["C"]))
plot(pig_betty, UD = UD1w_pHREML, ext = EXT)
title(expression("pHREML wAKDE"["C"]))

```

# All pigs

## Nest the telemetry objects

One row per pig, with the telemetry object in a list column. The movement models and home ranges are then added as further list columns.

```{r}

pigs_nested <- tibble(name = names(pig_data_ctmm),
                      telemetry = pig_data_ctmm)

pigs_nested

```

## Fit movement models and estimate home ranges

Model selection is slow, so the results are saved and re-loaded if they already exist. Delete the file to re-fit.

```{r}

hr_fits_file <- paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_nested_akde.rds")

if (file.exists(hr_fits_file)) {

  pigs_nested <- readRDS(hr_fits_file)

} else {

  tic()
  pigs_nested <- pigs_nested %>%
    mutate(
      # automated model guesstimate
      guess = map(telemetry, ~ ctmm.guess(.x, interactive = FALSE)),
      # model selection (defaults to pHREML)
      fit = map2(telemetry, guess, ~ ctmm.select(.x, .y)),
      # area-corrected AKDE
      ud = map2(telemetry, fit, ~ akde(.x, .y))
    )
  toc()

  saveRDS(pigs_nested, hr_fits_file)
  beep(sound = 2)

}

```

## Summarise the models and home range areas

```{r}

pigs_hr_summary <- pigs_nested %>%
  mutate(
    n_locations = map_int(telemetry, nrow),
    model = map_chr(fit, ~ summary(.x)$name),
    DOF_area = map_dbl(ud, ~ summary(.x)$DOF["area"]),
    # 95% home range area and CIs (units are reported in the column name)
    hr_area = map(ud, ~ {
      CI <- summary(.x)$CI
      tibble(units = rownames(CI), low = CI[1, "low"], est = CI[1, "est"], high = CI[1, "high"])
    })
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(name, n_locations, model, DOF_area, hr_area) %>%
  unnest(hr_area)

pigs_hr_summary

write_csv(pigs_hr_summary, paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_summary.csv"))

```

## Plot the home ranges

### Individually with ctmm

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4

pwalk(list(pigs_nested$name, pigs_nested$telemetry, pigs_nested$ud),
      function(name, telemetry, ud) {
        plot(telemetry, UD = ud)
        title(name)
      })

```

## Convert to sf and save for QGIS

`as.sf()` returns three polygons per pig for each contour level - the lower CI, the estimate and the upper CI. We extract the 50% (core area) and 95% (home range) contours. Each UD is in ctmm's own local projection, so they are all transformed to EPSG:3112 to match the rest of the data.

```{r}

# home range contours to extract
contour_levels <- c(0.5, 0.95)

pigs_hr_sf <- pigs_nested %>%
  dplyr::select(name, ud) %>%
  # one row per pig per contour level
  crossing(level_ud = contour_levels) %>%
  mutate(hr_sf = map2(ud, level_ud, ~ as.sf(.x, level.UD = .y, level = 0.95) %>%
                        st_transform(crs = 3112))) %>%
  dplyr::select(name, level_ud, hr_sf) %>%
  # as.sf already has a 'name' column (e.g. "Betty 95% est"), so rename it
  mutate(hr_sf = map(hr_sf, ~ rename(.x, contour = name))) %>%
  unnest(hr_sf) %>%
  mutate(ci = word(contour, -1)) %>%
  st_as_sf(crs = 3112)

pigs_hr_sf

# a single GeoPackage with all pigs (filter on 'level_ud' and 'ci' in QGIS)
st_write(pigs_hr_sf, paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde.gpkg"), delete_dsn = TRUE)

```

### All pigs together

```{r}

pigs_hr_sf %>%
  filter(ci == "est") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = pig_data, aes(x = x1_, y = y1_, colour = name),
             alpha = 0.1, size = 0.25) +
  # point estimates of the 50% (dashed) and 95% (solid) contours
  geom_sf(aes(colour = name, linetype = factor(level_ud)),
          fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual("Contour", values = c("0.5" = "dashed", "0.95" = "solid"),
                        labels = c("50%", "95%")) +
  coord_sf(datum = 3112) +
  labs(title = "50% and 95% AKDE home ranges", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave(paste0(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde.png"),
       width = 150, height = 150, units = "mm", scale = 1.25, dpi = 600)

```

## Plot interactively with leaflet

Each contour level is a separate layer that can be toggled in the layers control. The CIs and GPS fixes are hidden by default.

```{r}
#| label: leaflet-hr-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# reproject to WGS84 (EPSG:4326) for leaflet, and add the contour area
pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 <- pigs_hr_sf %>%
  mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(.)) / 1e6) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
  mutate(popup = paste0("ID: ", name,
                        "<br>Contour: ", level_ud * 100, "% (", ci, ")",
                        "<br>Area: ", round(area_km2, 2), " km<sup>2</sup>"))

hr_50_est <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.5, ci == "est")
hr_95_est <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.95, ci == "est")
hr_95_ci <- pigs_hr_sf_wgs84 %>% filter(level_ud == 0.95, ci != "est")

# GPS fixes (x1_/y1_ are in GDA94 / GA Lambert, EPSG:3112)
pig_map_pts <- pig_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(x1_), !is.na(y1_)) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x1_", "y1_"), crs = 3112) %>%
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

pal <- colorFactor(viridisLite::viridis(n_distinct(pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name), option = "H"),
                   domain = pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name)

hr_map <- leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
  addPolygons(data = hr_95_est,
              color = ~ pal(name), weight = 2, opacity = 1,
              fillColor = ~ pal(name), fillOpacity = 0.15,
              popup = ~ popup,
              highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 4, bringToFront = TRUE),
              group = "95% home range") %>%
  addPolygons(data = hr_50_est,
              color = ~ pal(name), weight = 2, opacity = 1,
              fillColor = ~ pal(name), fillOpacity = 0.35,
              popup = ~ popup,
              highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 4, bringToFront = TRUE),
              group = "50% core area") %>%
  addPolylines(data = hr_95_ci,
               color = ~ pal(name), weight = 1, opacity = 0.8,
               dashArray = "4 4",
               popup = ~ popup,
               group = "95% CIs") %>%
  # WebGL points, as there can be a lot of fixes
  leafgl::addGlPoints(data = pig_map_pts,
                      fillColor = pal(pig_map_pts$name),
                      fillOpacity = 0.75,
                      radius = 4,
                      popup = paste0("ID: ", pig_map_pts$name,
                                     "<br>Time: ", pig_map_pts$t1_),
                      group = "GPS fixes") %>%
  addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal,
            values = pigs_hr_sf_wgs84$name, title = "Pig ID") %>%
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft",
              options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE)) %>%
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("95% home range", "50% core area",
                                     "95% CIs", "GPS fixes"),
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) %>%
  hideGroup(c("95% CIs", "GPS fixes"))

# save a standalone copy to open in the browser (or share)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(hr_map, file.path(outputs_dir, "pigs_hr_akde_map.html"),
                        selfcontained = TRUE)

hr_map

```
